data.result:
I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. Here's a comprehensive setup guide:

## Server Setup

Run these commands on your server:

```bash
# Create directories
sudo mkdir -p /git/server
sudo mkdir -p /var/www/html
sudo chown $(whoami):$(whoami) /git/server /var/www/html

# Initialize bare git repository
cd /git/server
git init --bare

# Create the post-receive hook for automatic deployment
cat > /git/server/hooks/post-receive << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
DEPLOY_DIR="/var/www/html"
cd $DEPLOY_DIR
git --git-dir=/git/server --work-tree=$DEPLOY_DIR checkout -f
EOF

chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive

# Initialize the deployed directory with the repo
git clone --bare /git/server /tmp/init_repo
cd /var/www/html
git init
git remote add origin /git/server
```

## Web Server Setup

Choose one of these options:

### Option 1: Python (simplest)
```bash
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

### Option 2: Nginx (production-ready)
```bash
sudo apt-get install nginx
sudo tee /etc/nginx/sites-available/default > /dev/null << 'EOF'
server {
    listen 8080 default_server;
    server_name _;
    root /var/www/html;
    index index.html;
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
}
EOF

sudo systemctl restart nginx
```

## How it works

1. When you push to `origin master`, the post-receive hook runs automatically
2. It checks out the latest code into `/var/www/html`
3. The web server on port 8080 serves those files
4. `curl http://server:8080/hello.html` retrieves the file

## Client Side (your computer)

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server
cd server
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then verify from anywhere:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
# Output: hello world
```

The key piece is the **post-receive hook** in `/git/server/hooks/post-receive` — it automatically deploys changes to the web directory whenever you push.

```bash
git clone --bare /git/server /tmp/init_repo

```

## Web Server Setup

Choose one of these options:

### Option 1: Python (simplest)
```bash
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

### Option 2: Nginx (production-ready)
```bash
sudo apt-get install nginx
sudo tee /etc/nginx/sites-available/default > /dev/null << 'EOF'
server {
    listen 8080 default_server;
    server_name _;
    root /var/www/html;
    index index.html;
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
}
EOF

sudo systemctl restart nginx
```

## How it works

1. When you push to `origin master`, the post-receive hook runs automatically
2. It checks out the latest code into `/var/www/html`
3. The web server on port 8080 serves those files
4. `curl http://server:8080/hello.html` retrieves the file

## Client Side (your computer)

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server
cd server
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then verify from anywhere:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
# Output: hello world
```

The key piece is the **post-receive hook** in `/git/server/hooks/post-receive` — it automatically deploys changes to the web directory whenever you push.
